new_rules.name: stretch-head-of-own-two-vs-side-press
new_rules.text: When an opponent stone presses beside the head stone of your two-stone line, stretch one point straight out at the head so they cannot hane at the head of two stones.
new_rules.label: A0g1p3

new_rules.name: capture-abandoned-armpit-stone
new_rules.text: Capturing a lone opponent stone left in atari in the armpit of your own bend, after they played far away, is usually slow; take the big point first.
new_rules.label: A0g1p11

new_rules.name: kosumi-link-extension-of-lone-two-lib-stone
new_rules.text: Extend your lone two-liberty stone onto a point diagonal to another of your stones, with both linking points empty, so it gains a liberty and is miai-connected instead of being chased alone.
new_rules.label: B0g1p29

new_rules.name: one-two-point-contact-in-corner
new_rules.text: On the corner 1-2 point, with the 1-1 point empty, a first-line move touching an opponent stone (a block of their edge crawl or a hane under their 2-2 stone) is often the key liberty or eye-space point of a corner fight.
new_rules.label: A0g1p35

new_rules.name: corner-2-1-under-crowded-2-2-block
new_rules.text: In a crowded corner where the 2-2, 3-2, 2-3 and 3-3 points are all occupied, the empty 2-1 point beneath them is a vital eye and liberty point for both sides.
new_rules.label: B0g1p33

new_rules.name: connect-cut-lone-two-lib-stone-to-line
new_rules.text: When the opponent already holds one link point between your lone two-liberty stone and your line of stones, connect solidly at the other link point before they atari and cut there.
new_rules.label: B0g1p33

new_rules.name: first-line-block-end-of-opp-crawl-under-wall
new_rules.text: Block on the first line at the end of the opponent's first-line crawl of two or more stones, when your own second-line stone sits right above their end stone, so they cannot push further along the edge.
new_rules.label: B0g1p37

new_rules.name: edge-hane-under-strong-opp-boundary-stone
new_rules.text: On the first line, play directly under the opponent's second-line stone of a big safe chain when your own stone touches it diagonally; this edge hane or push settles the boundary and is bigger than it looks.
new_rules.label: B0g1p41

new_rules.name: complete-cut-through-knights-move
new_rules.text: When your stone already sits on one of the two middle points of the opponent's knight's move, play the other middle point to cut their stones apart.
new_rules.label: B0g2p6

new_rules.name: attach-lone-stone-with-jump-support
new_rules.text: Attach beside a lone opponent stone when your own stone sits a one-point jump behind the contact point, perpendicular to the contact, so the attachment is backed up and claims the side.
new_rules.label: B0g2p4

new_rules.name: atari-crosscut-stone-from-outside
new_rules.text: Ataring the opponent's lone two-liberty crosscutting stone from outside is usually slow even when the ladder works, because your own cut stones stay weak; take the big shape point instead.
new_rules.label: A0g2p12

new_rules.name: hane-head-of-parallel-opp-two
new_rules.text: When your two-stone line and their two-stone line stand side by side, hane at the head of their pair, diagonally beyond your own head stone, before they hane at yours.
new_rules.label: B0g2p12

new_rules.name: diagonal-move-beside-own-atari-stone-liberty
new_rules.text: When your lone stone is in atari, a move diagonal to it right beside its last liberty neither saves it nor threatens much; the opponent simply captures, so escape or play elsewhere.
new_rules.label: A0g2p18

new_rules.name: second-line-kosumi-under-opp-third-line-stone
new_rules.text: On the second line, the empty point diagonally under an opponent's third-line stone, with the points between them and toward the edge empty, undermines its base and is a big quiet move.
new_rules.label: A0g2p18

new_rules.name: extend-two-lib-group-to-three-libs
new_rules.text: When your chain of two or more stones is down to two liberties, extending it so it has three or more liberties is usually more urgent than a hane or a move elsewhere.
new_rules.label: A0g2p20

new_rules.name: fill-liberty-of-big-three-lib-chain
new_rules.text: When a large opponent chain of five or more stones is down to three liberties, taking one of those liberties (without self-atari) is usually the urgent move of a capturing race, ahead of side ataris on small chains.
new_rules.label: A0g2p28

new_rules.name: edge-connect-across-opp-cut
new_rules.text: On the first line, connect your edge stone to your own stone directly above it when an opponent stone sits on the cutting diagonal and one of the chains is short of liberties; it removes the cut and atari before capturing elsewhere.
new_rules.label: B0g2p28

new_rules.name: lone-stone-in-armpit-of-strong-chain
new_rules.text: A lone stone dropped into the inner corner of a strong opponent chain's bend, with no friendly stone around, gets only two liberties and is simply ataried; it is a poor invasion or reduction point.
new_rules.label: B0g2p38

new_rules.name: butt-between-own-and-opp-jump-stones
new_rules.text: In open space, the empty point directly between your healthy stone and a healthy opponent stone a one-point jump away butts head-on into their stone; it strengthens both and is usually a poor move.
new_rules.label: B1g1p6

new_rules.name: second-line-base-under-own-fourth-line-stone
new_rules.text: A second-line move with all eight neighbours empty, two lines below your own fourth-line stone (straight or one point along), makes a base for a weak group and is bigger than nearby contact moves.
new_rules.label: A1g1p11

new_rules.name: bare-second-line-cut-at-sole-link-two-libs
new_rules.text: Cutting directly at the single second-line link point between their edge stone and their third-line stone, when the cutting stone gets only two liberties, is premature: they atari from the open side and the cutter dies.
new_rules.label: A1g1p23

new_rules.name: corner-2-2-under-own-pincered-2-3-stone
new_rules.text: Play the corner 2-2 point directly under your own lone stone on the 2-3 point when an opponent stone stands a one-point jump from it along the third line; it gives the invading stone a base and eye shape in their corner.
new_rules.label: A1g1p25

new_rules.name: block-under-own-3rd-line-stone-vs-gap-probe
new_rules.text: When their second-line probe sits diagonally under your third-line stone, block on the second line directly under your own stone, beside the probe, so it cannot slide under you.
new_rules.label: B1g1p22

new_rules.name: slow-capture-of-sealed-dead-stones
new_rules.text: Capturing opponent stones in atari whose last liberty lies between two of your own stones is usually slow: extending there would not save them, so they are already dead; play the big or vital point first.
new_rules.label: B1g1p28

new_rules.name: atari-dead-chain-between-own-stones
new_rules.text: Ataring an opponent chain of 2-5 stones that is already ladder-dead, on a point between two of your own stones and away from their last move, is usually a slow gote move; the stones are dead anyway.
new_rules.label: B1g1p30

new_rules.name: slow-capture-of-abandoned-inland-stones
new_rules.text: Capturing 1-3 inland opponent stones that they left in atari while playing elsewhere is usually slow; they were given up, so play the urgent point first.
new_rules.label: B1g1p30
